tests.procedure: Under strong white light check each received sample container separately on a clean transparent watch glass or glass dish for foreign particles, colour and conformity with the visual specification.

details.reference: BP 2024 Monograph for Calcium Hydrogen Phosphate Dihydrate

tests.source: Calcium Hydrogen Phosphate Dihydrate__New 1-2_STM Calcium Hydrogen Phosphate Dihydrate - New.txt:30

tests.procedure: BP-style stepwise solubility: 100 mg sample in a stoppered tube with 0.1 mL solvent, shake 1 min, hold 25.0 ± 0.5 °C for 15 min (repeat once if not dissolved); add 0.9 mL, then 2 mL, then 7 mL solvent with the same shake and hold to classify very soluble / freely soluble / soluble / sparingly soluble; if still undissolved, 10 mg in 10 mL (slightly soluble), then 1 mg in 10 mL (very slightly soluble), else practically insoluble. Repeat with methanol, ethanol (96 per cent), dilute nitric acid and dilute hydrochloric acid.

solvents: first solvent not named in the STM (see openQuestions)
details.reference: BP (SC IV K.) Characters Section in Monographs (Hygroscopicity and Solubility)

tests.source: Calcium Hydrogen Phosphate Dihydrate__New 1-2_STM Calcium Hydrogen Phosphate Dihydrate - New.txt:31

tests.procedure: Identification (BP 2024): test 1: dissolve 0.1 g with heating in 10 mL dilute hydrochloric acid, add 2.5 mL dilute ammonia R1, shake, add 5 mL of a 35 g/L ammonium oxalate solution; a white precipitate is produced. Test 2: dissolve 0.1 g in 5 mL dilute nitric acid, add 2 mL ammonium molybdate solution, heat at 70 °C for 2 min; a yellow precipitate is produced.

test1.sample: 0.1 g in 10 mL dilute hydrochloric acid, heated

test2.sample: 0.1 g in 5 mL dilute nitric acid

details.reference: BP 2024 Monograph for Calcium Hydrogen Phosphate Dihydrate

tests.source: Calcium Hydrogen Phosphate Dihydrate__New 1-2_STM Calcium Hydrogen Phosphate Dihydrate - New.txt:32

tests.procedure: Acid-insoluble substances (BP 2024): dissolve 5.0 g in 40 mL water (W1); add 10 mL hydrochloric acid, heat to boiling for 5 min, cool; collect the insoluble substances on ashless filter paper; wash until no turbidity forms when silver nitrate solution R2 is added to the filtrate; ignite at 600 ± 50 °C. The residue must weigh not more than 10 mg. % = residue / W1 x 100.

details.reference: BP 2024 Monograph for Calcium Hydrogen Phosphate Dihydrate

tests.source: Calcium Hydrogen Phosphate Dihydrate__New 1-2_STM Calcium Hydrogen Phosphate Dihydrate - New.txt:33

tests.procedure: Chlorides limit test (BP 2024 Appendix VII): test solution 0.20 g dissolved in 20 mL water and 13 mL dilute nitric acid, diluted to 100 mL, filtered if necessary; 50 mL used. Reference: 0.70 mL 0.01 M hydrochloric acid, 6 mL dilute nitric acid, diluted to 50 mL with water. Add 1 mL silver nitrate solution R2 to each and mix; after 5 min protected from light the opalescence of the test is not more intense than the reference. Limit NMT 0.25%.

details.testSample: 0.20 g in 20 mL water + 13 mL dilute nitric acid, to 100 mL; 50 mL used
details.reference: 0.70 mL 0.01 M hydrochloric acid + 6 mL dilute nitric acid to 50 mL

tests.source: Calcium Hydrogen Phosphate Dihydrate__New 1-2_STM Calcium Hydrogen Phosphate Dihydrate - New.txt:34

tests.procedure: Carbonates: shake 0.5 g with 5 mL carbon dioxide-free water, add 1 mL hydrochloric acid. No effervescence is produced.

details.reference: BP 2024 Monograph for Calcium Hydrogen Phosphate Dihydrate

tests.source: Calcium Hydrogen Phosphate Dihydrate__New 1-2_STM Calcium Hydrogen Phosphate Dihydrate - New.txt:35

tests.procedure: Sulfates limit test (BP 2024): test solution 0.5 g in 5 mL water and 5 mL dilute hydrochloric acid, diluted to 100 mL, filtered if necessary; 20 mL + 1 mL dilute hydrochloric acid, diluted to 50 mL. Reference: 1.0 mL 0.005 M sulfuric acid + 1 mL dilute hydrochloric acid, diluted to 50 mL, filtered if necessary. Add 2 mL of 120 g/L barium chloride solution to each; stand 10 min; any opalescence in the test is not more intense than the reference. Limit NMT 0.5%.

details.testSample: 0.5 g in 5 mL water + 5 mL dilute hydrochloric acid, to 100 mL; 20 mL + 1 mL dilute hydrochloric acid to 50 mL
details.reference: 1.0 mL 0.005 M sulfuric acid + 1 mL dilute hydrochloric acid to 50 mL
details.bariumChloride: 2 mL of 120 g/L barium chloride solution
details.reference2: BP 2024 Monograph for Calcium Hydrogen Phosphate Dihydrate

tests.source: Calcium Hydrogen Phosphate Dihydrate__New 1-2_STM Calcium Hydrogen Phosphate Dihydrate - New.txt:36

tests.procedure: Arsenic limit test, Method A (BP 2024 Appendix VII): test solution 2 mL of solution S in a conical flask, diluted to 25 mL with water; add 15 mL hydrochloric acid, 0.1 mL stannous chloride solution and 5 mL potassium iodide solution, stand 15 min; add 5 g activated zinc, assemble the apparatus immediately and immerse the flask in a water-bath. Reference: 1 mL arsenic standard solution (1 ppm As) diluted to 25 mL and treated the same way. After at least 2 h the colour of the test is not more intense than the standard. Limit NMT 10 ppm. The STM's alternative AAS method is not transcribed.

details.solutionS: 2.5 g in 20 mL dilute hydrochloric acid, precipitate with dilute ammonia R1, redissolve with dilute hydrochloric acid, dilute to 50 mL with distilled water
details.referenceStandard: 1 mL arsenic standard solution (1 ppm As) to 25 mL
details.reference: BP Appendix VII Limit Tests, Arsenic (Method A)

tests.source: Calcium Hydrogen Phosphate Dihydrate__New 1-2_STM Calcium Hydrogen Phosphate Dihydrate - New.txt:37

tests.procedure: Barium: to 0.5 g add 10 mL water and heat to boiling; while stirring add 1 mL hydrochloric acid dropwise; cool and filter if necessary; add 2 mL of a 10 g/L dipotassium sulfate solution; stand 10 min. No turbidity is produced.

details.reagent: 2 mL of 10 g/L dipotassium sulfate solution
details.reference: BP 2024 Monograph for Calcium Hydrogen Phosphate Dihydrate

tests.source: Calcium Hydrogen Phosphate Dihydrate__New 1-2_STM Calcium Hydrogen Phosphate Dihydrate - New.txt:38

tests.procedure: Iron limit test (BP 2024 Appendix VII): test solution 0.5 mL of solution S diluted to 10 mL with water; add 2 mL of 200 g/L citric acid monohydrate and 0.1 mL thioglycolic acid, mix, make alkaline with ammonia, dilute to 20 mL. Reference: 10 mL iron standard solution (1 ppm Fe) with the same reagents. After 5 min any pink colour in the test is not more intense than the standard. Limit NMT 400 ppm.

details.testSolution: 0.5 mL solution S to 10 mL water
details.referenceSolution: 10 mL iron standard solution (1 ppm Fe)
details.reference2: BP Appendix VII Limit Tests, Iron

tests.source: Calcium Hydrogen Phosphate Dihydrate__New 1-2_STM Calcium Hydrogen Phosphate Dihydrate - New.txt:39

tests.procedure: Loss on ignition (BP 2024): weigh an empty crucible previously ignited at 800-825 °C and cooled in desiccator (W0); weigh accurately 1.000 g into it (W1); ignite in a calibrated muffle at 800-825 °C for 2 h, cool in desiccator, weigh (W2); repeat to constant weight. % loss on ignition = (W1 - W2) / (W1 - W0) x 100.

details.reference: BP 2024 Monograph for Calcium Hydrogen Phosphate Dihydrate

tests.source: Calcium Hydrogen Phosphate Dihydrate__New 1-2_STM Calcium Hydrogen Phosphate Dihydrate - New.txt:40

tests.procedure: Assay (BP Appendix VIII D, complexometric back titration): dissolve 0.4 g in 12 mL dilute hydrochloric acid (heat on water-bath if needed), dilute to 200 mL with water. Transfer 20.0 mL to a flask, add 25.0 mL of 0.02 M sodium edetate, 50 mL water, 5 mL ammonium chloride buffer solution pH 10.7 and about 25 mg mordant black 11 triturate; titrate the excess sodium edetate with 0.02 M zinc sulfate; blank titration. 1 mL of 0.02 M sodium edetate = 3.44 mg of calcium hydrogen phosphate dihydrate. Assay = (E.P x eq.wt x F x 100) / Wt.

details.solvent: 12 mL dilute hydrochloric acid, dilute to 200 mL
details.buffer: 5 mL ammonium chloride buffer solution pH 10.7
details.eqWt: 3.44 mg per mL of 0.02 M sodium edetate
details.formula: Assay = (E.P x eq.wt x F x 100) / Wt; E.P end point (mL), eq.wt 3.44 mg, F titrant factor, Wt sample weight (g) as written
details.titrantStandardization: 0.02 M disodium edetate VS: 7.444 g disodium edetate in 1000 mL; standardise against 0.100 g zinc in 4 mL 7 M hydrochloric acid, diluted to 100 mL, 25 mL to 200 mL, xylenol orange triturate and hexamine, titrate to yellow; 1 mL = 1.308 mg Zn
details.reference: BP Appendix VIII D Complexometric Titrations; BP 2024 Monograph for Calcium Hydrogen Phosphate Dihydrate

tests.procedure: Particle size distribution: calibrated analytical sieving or particle size analyser; measure mass percentage in each sieve size range. In-house specification: D10 125 µm (10% pass through 120 mesh); D50 250 µm (50% pass through 60 mesh); D90 500 µm (90% pass through 35 mesh).

details.method: calibrated analytical sieving or particle size analyser
details.reference: In-house specification by R&D department for PSD

tests.source: Calcium Hydrogen Phosphate Dihydrate__New 1-2_STM Calcium Hydrogen Phosphate Dihydrate - New.txt:42

tests.procedure: Microbial enumeration (USP <2021>): weigh 10 g sample into a sterile container and complete to 100 mL with soyabean casein digest broth (SCDB); within 1 h pipette 1 mL of the dilution into each of four plates, two with SCDA (TAMC) and two with SDA (TYMC). Incubate SCDA 24-72 h at 30-35 °C. Total CFU/g = (colonies on the two plates / 2) x DF (10); if no colonies from the lowest dilution, report less than 10.

details.limit: Not more than 10^3 CFU/gm (STM prints 103, superscript lost; spec sheet NMT 1000 CFU/g, loaded)

tests.source: Calcium Hydrogen Phosphate Dihydrate__New 1-2_STM Calcium Hydrogen Phosphate Dihydrate - New.txt:44

tests.procedure: Microbial enumeration (USP <2021>): as for TAMC; the two SDA plates are incubated 5-7 days at 20-25 °C; total yeasts and molds CFU/g = (colonies on the two plates / 2) x DF (10).

details.limit: Not more than 10^2 CFU/gm (STM prints 102, superscript lost; spec sheet NMT 100 CFU/g, loaded)

tests.source: Calcium Hydrogen Phosphate Dihydrate__New 1-2_STM Calcium Hydrogen Phosphate Dihydrate - New.txt:44

tests.procedure: Specified microorganism E. coli (USP <2022>): incubate SCDB 30-35 °C 24-48 h; transfer 1 mL to 10 mL MacConkey broth, 42-44 °C 24-48 h; subculture both on MacConkey agar, 30-35 °C 18-24 h; brick red colonies (possibly with a zone of precipitated bile) indicate possible E. coli; confirm by Gram stain (gram-negative short rods), EMB (dark-centred colonies with or without metallic sheen) and TBX (blue or green colonies, 42-44 °C 18-72 h); if possible confirm with an identification system (report if probability above 70%). Limit absent in 10 g.
